newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-EU finmins reach budget, jobs deal.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-EU finmins reach budget, jobs deal.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' views on news that EU finance ministers have reached agreement on a budget stability pact for countries joining the single currency and a resolution on jobs and growth.
PAUL HORNE, CHIEF INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, SMITH BARNEY

For bond markets it will be helpful but we've already seen yields going south and yield spreads saying the same. The effects depend on what the word "resolution" means. I feel certain the Germans are not going to give anything away on infrastructural spending.
ROB HAYWARD, ECONOMIC ADVISER, BANK OF AMERICA

"It's not that much of a surprise given that at the end of the day neither France nor Germany could allow the whole thing to fail. It lets France go back and say we have done something and the Germans go back and say we haven't given in to anything. But given that it is a fudged compromise, it is not great for European currencies against the dollar, and not good for core European assets relative to those in the U.S.
TEIS KNUTHSEN, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, FIRST CHICAGO

"It's positive for the market to get the jobs agreement because that is essentially what's already been priced in. "I fail to see how this will improve unemployment in Europe as that is a structural problem. But it does put EMU on track for 1999."
DAVID BRICKMAN, EUROPEAN ECONOMIST, YAMAICHI INT'L

One could argue that the stability pact will actually make it a strong euro. This is the most rigid set of fiscal rules in the world, and on that basis it is difficult to argue that the euro is going to be a soft currency.

On bonds, It's mostly been priced into the market. I don't think it's too much of a surprise. If anything we've actually seen a bit of profit taking on the news. The upside from here is limited but peripheral countries may benefit more than the core.

"We've had a view all along that it wasn't going to be something as 'technical' as the stability pact that would be able to derail this summit, but you've got to remember there's no smoke without fire. I think what we're seeing is the practical reality of EMU and the philosophical differences between France and Germany.
If markets were in a state of semi-paralysis prior to this resolution, I'm pretty sure they'll remain in a state of semi-paralysis."
